entry.title: The Knickknack Peddler
entry.blurb: Painted during the reign of emperor Ningzong, the drama unfolding around vulnerable children may allude to Ningzong’s nine sons who died young, leaving him without a direct male descendant.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund

facts: The court artist Li Song from Hangzhou excelled in meticulous depictions of children, peddlers, and their various goods.
Here, he captures a dramatic scene of children attacking a snake with a stick and stone.
The peddler rushes toward the children, leaving his merchandise unattended.
